verdict.rationale: Proton's own CLI announcement says the Proton Pass CLI works in CI/CD, servers, containers, and headless environments. It also says the CLI can inject credentials into scripts, deployments, and pipelines without exposing secrets in plaintext, logs, or history, which directly covers headless and CI automation. The evidence comes only from a launch blog post, though, so the operational details are thin. Missing for 10: documentation of non-interactive authentication for CI (e.g., service tokens), install and command reference docs, and independent or hands-on corroboration of headless and CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Work in CI/CD, servers, containers, and headless environments
With Proton Pass CLI, credentials can be injected directly into scripts, deployments, and CI/CD pipelines without exposing secrets in plaintext, shell, logs, or command history.
the CLI enables you to securely retrieve secrets and other items across scripts, deployments, and continuous integration/ continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines.
